failure_summary.description: Search or refinement results were not consistently bound and saved to cache.
Agents treated a new constraint as a no-op, selected an unsupported cache key, or repeated unrelated work.
Agents skipped an actionable domain when another domain lacked information, or failed to derive hotel checkout from a stated stay length.
Agents changed a user-supplied category, confused a fitness preference, or encoded a round trip as one flight search.
Agents imported tools instead of calling the provided functions directly.

patch.reasoning: Most cache and tool-use failures already contradict explicit skill guidance, so repeating those instructions would not address a skill gap. The missing-information rule, however, currently blocks valid work in complete domains and omits deriving checkout from an explicit stay length. A separate clarification preserves user-supplied category values rather than normalizing them to near-synonyms.

edits.target:
## Missing mandatory information
Before searching, check the full conversation for all mandatory inputs required by each requested tool. If any are missing, do not invent values, use defaults, or run a partial search. Make one `seek_information` call asking only for the missing mandatory information across the requested domains; optional preferences are not mandatory inputs.
edits.content:
## Missing mandatory information
Check mandatory inputs separately for each requested action and domain. If an action lacks required information, do not search that action; make one `seek_information` call asking only for its missing mandatory inputs. Still execute and cache other requested actions whose own mandatory inputs are complete. For a hotel stay with an exact check-in date and an explicitly stated length in nights, use `adjust_date` to derive checkout; do not ask for a checkout date that can be derived this way. Never invent values or use defaults, and do not treat vague timing as an exact date.

edits.target: ## Validate tool arguments and preserve user intent
edits.content: - Preserve user-supplied entity names and category values when passing tool arguments. Do not normalize, translate, or replace them with near-synonyms; use the schema to choose the argument field, not to rewrite the value.
